quranicProvenance.duaText: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
quranicProvenance.orthographyDecision: Rendered in standard MSA orthography (إِلَهَ, not the mushaf dagger-alif إِلَٰهَ). Reviewer/pipeline to confirm the convention for embedded Qur'anic quotes; no sura:aya display widget was invented.
quranicProvenance.level: إنّ (inna-wa-akhawatuha) and كان (kana-wa-akhawatuha) are Level-2 structures, admitted here only because this is a verbatim du'a A1 learners already know by heart. Glossed word-by-word; not expected for production.

reviewerFlags.issue: Anger simplified to 'with his people'; Qur'an has مُغَاضِبًا (21:87). Theological question of a prophet leaving is deliberately left untouched.
Falling into the sea simplifies the casting of lots (37:141). Confirm the simplification, or approve the alternative رَمَى الرِّجَالُ يُونُسَ فِي الْبَحْرِ.
'The whale brought Yunus out' is the conventional children's phrasing; Qur'an states Allah as agent (فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِالْعَرَاءِ, 37:145). Flag if agency should be stated as Allah's command.
Return -> belief order follows the common narrative (37:147-148); mufassirun differ on exact chronology relative to 10:98. Not asserted dogmatically.
حُوت rendered 'whale / great fish' (balina / büyük balık); glosses stay non-committal on species.

possibleChapter2: Epilogue (37:146): the يَقْطِين (gourd) plant, the tasbih in the three darknesses, and the 'hundred thousand or more' (37:147) — omitted at A1, available if a longer read is wanted.
